source.title: Prelude in C♯ minor, Op. 3 No. 2

bars.description: Play the pickup, then printed bars 1–61 once; returns are written out, with no inserted repeat.

endpoints.basis: The first A-octave attack is near 1.55 s, before the G-sharp attack near 2.72 s selected by the broad search. The final pianissimo chord near 205.8 s reattacks the same upper voicing as the penultimate chord near 203.25 s; the original endpoint incorrectly selected that earlier chord. Absolute-pitch features confirm the original source register, without the separate 1921 transfer's nominal-semitone correction.

anchors.label: third-opening-C-sharp-octaves
anchors.basis: The third opening bell is C-sharp1/C-sharp2/C-sharp3 near 4.2 s. The unconstrained long hold began before its measured attack. This is an inspected fitting constraint, not independent validation.

anchors.label: coda-first-chord-A3-A4-signature
anchors.basis: The first coda voicing's A3/A4 signature appears near179.04s. The old numeric pass placed it184.554s, several seconds into later coda material. The five distinct chromatic signatures establish the source order; these are fitting constraints, not independent validation.

anchors.label: coda-second-chord-A-sharp3-G-sharp4-signature
anchors.basis: The second chord's A-sharp3/G-sharp4 pair peaks near183.02s, not the old187.857s assignment. A nearby detected onset alone does not establish the correct voicing.

anchors.label: coda-third-chord-G3-A4-signature
anchors.basis: The third coda chord's G3/A4 signature peaks near187.40s. Preserve the full progression instead of compressing its first three chords into the later quiet tail.

anchors.label: coda-fourth-chord-F-sharp-A-sharp-signature
anchors.basis: The fourth source voicing's F-sharp/A-sharp pairs are visible near192.20s, following the G3/A4 chord and preceding the D-sharp/F-sharp/A chord.

anchors.label: coda-fifth-chord-D-sharp-F-sharp-A-signature
anchors.basis: The fifth coda voicing's D-sharp/F-sharp/A combination is visible near197.28s in logarithmic pitch features. Historical noise limits individual-note certainty, not the observed chord sequence.

anchors.label: closing-lower-C-sharp-minor-voicing
anchors.basis: The lower closing voicing's G-sharp3/G-sharp4 pair peaks near200.96s, before the higher203.24s chord and separate final205.67s reattack. Retain all three written attacks.

anchors.label: penultimate-upper-C-sharp-minor-chord
anchors.basis: The written eighth-note upper chord near 203.25 s precedes a distinct final pianissimo reattack near 205.8 s. Their identical pitch classes had let the broad endpoint pick the earlier chord. Both source attacks remain; this is fitting evidence, not independent or aural validation.

provenance: Source MIDI tracks were inspected against the named score staves; staff labels do not claim contrapuntal voice separation. EXT: Bosworth 1896 and Universal 1910 piano editions. The source identifies the complete solo-piano Op. 3 No. 2, not Rachmaninoff's physical performing edition.
